subject: A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability and Cordis, draft of August 13, 2026
central_claim: Cordis is a publishable AI engineering topic because the August 13, 2026 active-revision preprint, public Cordis implementation, DeepSeek Harness documentation and Koishi case study support a bounded E2 claim: explicit plugin dependencies and reversible context effects can narrow AI maintenance, testing, replacement and recovery scope, while Cordis itself is not evidence of autonomous self-improvement.

selection.reason: The topic affects agent harness and plugin-heavy application architecture decisions. It is new as an August 13, 2026 preprint and public implementation package, is verifiable through multiple primary source URLs, and helps SW engineers decide how to separate stable cores from AI-editable adapters and workflow plugins.

signals.note: The topic was fixed by the editor. Search and popularity signals were not used to replace the subject.
Opened the public paper repository README. It states the paper title, draft date of August 13, 2026, active-revision preprint status, and links to paper.pdf.

Downloaded the PDF and extracted text with npx pdf-parse. It identifies authors Yifan Shi, Wei Zhang and Tianyi Cui with Peking University and DeepSeek-AI affiliations, defines the two dimensions, describes the Cordis implementation, and leaves self-evolving harness validation as future work.

Opened the implementation repository and checked HEAD 8cc9e33fab69e2d0476d126baaf2acb24e6a6ab4. README describes Cordis as a meta-framework of spatiotemporal composability and warns that the API is not stable.

Opened the public repository and README. It states that DeepSeek Harness is an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek AI, uses an everything-is-a-plugin architecture, and is powered by Cordis.
Opened the public primer and matching raw markdown. It describes plugins, contexts, service dependencies through inject, typed events, and reversible registrations through ctx.effect()/ctx.on().

Opened the public Koishi repository. README describes a TypeScript chatbot framework and an ecosystem with over 3000 official and community plugins; the Cordis paper case study states over 4000 community plugins and notes the observational limits.

claims.claim: Cordis formalizes temporal composability as reverting component side effects on removal and spatial composability as declaring and reactively managing component dependencies.
claims.version: README and PDF at repository HEAD 948a07b369c62adb3b12e102458be5c18dfb69b9
claims.method: Read paper README, abstract and introduction pages extracted from PDF.
limitations: Definitions are from the authors' preprint and not independent validation of utility.
conflict_of_interest: The paper repository and PDF are author/project primary sources.

claims.claim: Cordis implements the model through context, fibers, ctx.effect cleanup tracking, inject-based service dependency declarations, component lifecycle, configuration reconciliation and hot module replacement.
claims.version: Cordis HEAD 8cc9e33fab69e2d0476d126baaf2acb24e6a6ab4; Harness vendored API docs at HEAD 47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a
claims.method: Read paper implementation section, Cordis README, Harness generated Fiber API and Registry API docs.
limitations: Article did not run Cordis test suite or independently benchmark HMR/reconciliation behavior.
conflict_of_interest: Cordis and Harness docs are project primary sources.

claims.claim: DeepSeek Harness is powered by Cordis and documents a plugin architecture where model adapters, tool registry, session log and agent loop are replaceable plugins or services.
claims.method: Read Harness README, Cordis primer and architecture document.
limitations: Confirms architecture and adoption, not autonomous self-improvement performance.
conflict_of_interest: DeepSeek Harness documentation is a project primary source.

claims.claim: The Koishi case study is observational evidence from one TypeScript ecosystem, not a controlled runtime-overhead or productivity comparison, and Koishi uses Cordis v3 while the paper presents Cordis v4.

claims.claim: Cordis can support AI maintenance by narrowing the component scope AI must inspect, test, replace and recover, but it is not itself an autonomous self-improvement engine.
